content:
Three litres of water weigh three kilos, and that is why hiking backpacks in Nairobi should be chosen by size and fit before brand or colour. A 20-30 litre daypack covers Ngong Hills, Mt Longonot and most day hikes, 35-50 litres suits an overnight camp, and 55-70 litres carries your own kit up Mt Kenya.

Plenty of hikers buy the pack that looked good on a hook, then spend five hours fighting it: straps cutting into the shoulders, a sweaty back, a jacket snagging on whistling thorn. Below: how to pick the volume, measure your torso, adjust the straps, judge a thrifted pack, load it and care for it, plus where to try one on in Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Day hikes: a 20-30 litre daypack holds 2-3 litres of water, lunch, a rain layer and a fleece
  • Overnight camping: 35-50 litres fits a sleeping bag, mat, stove and food for one night
  • Multi-day treks: 55-70 litres suits Mt Kenya if you carry your own tent and food
  • Fit: pack size follows torso length, measured from the C7 neck bone to the top of the hip bones, not your height
  • Weather: carry a rain cover or liner in the long rains (March-May) and short rains (October-December)
  • Where to buy: try hiking backpacks in Nairobi at Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, Nairobi, or order online with M-Pesa or cash on delivery

What Size Hiking Backpack Do You Need?

Choosing between hiking backpacks in Nairobi starts with how long you are out and what you must carry. A day hike needs 20-30 litres, an overnight trip 35-50 litres, and a multi-day trek with your own tent and food 55-70 litres.

Volume is measured in litres and includes the main compartment and pockets. Bigger is not better: a half-empty 60 litre pack sags and pulls you backwards on steep ground, while an overstuffed 20 litre pack forces gear onto the outside where it swings and catches on bush. When comparing hiking backpacks in Nairobi, choose the size for the trips you do most often, not for the single big trek you might do next year.

Is a 25 litre daypack enough for a day hike near Nairobi?

A 25 litre daypack is enough for almost every day hike near Nairobi. It takes two to three litres of water, lunch, a rain jacket, a fleece and a small first aid kit, with space left for a headlamp in case you finish after dark.

Among hiking backpacks in Nairobi, a daypack with a hydration sleeve helps on hot, exposed hikes such as the Mt Longonot crater rim, where shade is scarce and you need to sip often. Our Mt Longonot hike guide explains why water ends up being the heaviest thing in most day packs on that trail.

What size backpack do you need for Mt Kenya?

For Mt Kenya you need a 55-70 litre pack if you carry your own tent, sleeping bag and food, or a 25-35 litre daypack if porters carry your main bag. Most organised Mt Kenya climbs use porters, so ask your operator first.

With porters, your main kit travels in a duffel and your daypack holds water, snacks, a warm jacket, gloves and rain gear. Our list of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya splits everything between the two bags, and the same logic applies to Kilimanjaro, where our post on buying Kilimanjaro gear in Nairobi covers the summit layers your daypack must hold on the final night.

Daypack, Hydration Pack or Trekking Pack: Which Suits Your Hikes?

Among hiking backpacks in Nairobi, a daypack suits most hikers, a hydration pack suits fast or hot hikes where you want to drink on the move, and a trekking pack only makes sense if you camp or carry your own kit for several days.

The three types overlap: many daypacks take a water bladder, and some hydration packs carry 15 litres or more. What matters is how much you carry and how far.

Hydration pack3 L bladder plus 2-15 L storageTrail runs, Karura loops, hot crater rimsLittle room for a fleece and lunch
Daypack20-30 LNgong Hills, Longonot, Kinangop and most club hikesThin hip belt, so heavy loads sit on the shoulders
Trekking pack50-70 LSelf-supported Mt Kenya, Aberdares campingHeavy and bulky on a simple day hike

How Do You Choose Hiking Backpacks in Nairobi That Fit?

Choose hiking backpacks in Nairobi by torso length and hip size, not by height or looks. A pack that fits rests most of its load on your hips, so your shoulders and lower back stay comfortable for hours.

Two people of the same height can need different pack sizes because torso length varies a lot. Most larger hiking backpacks in Nairobi come in sizes (S, M, L) or have an adjustable back system, while most small daypacks come in one size that suits a wide range of people. Women's-specific packs usually have a shorter back, narrower and more curved shoulder straps, and a more angled hip belt.

How do you measure your torso length for a backpack?

Measure from the bony bump at the base of your neck (the C7 vertebra) down to an imaginary line between the tops of your hip bones (the iliac crest). Ask a friend to measure along your spine with a soft tape while you stand straight.

  1. Tilt your head forward and find the most prominent bone where your neck meets your shoulders.
  2. Put your hands on your hips, slide them down until they rest on the top of your hip bones, and point your thumbs backwards.
  3. Have a friend measure along your spine from the neck bone to the line between your thumbs.
  4. Compare the result with the torso range on the pack's label or the maker's size chart, as ranges differ between brands.

In what order should you adjust the straps on a hiking backpack?

Adjust the hip belt first, then the shoulder straps, then the load lifters, and finally the sternum strap. Whichever hiking backpacks in Nairobi you shortlist, loosen everything first and load 5-7 kg so the pack behaves as it will on the trail.

  1. Hip belt: padding on top of your hip bones, snug but not pinching.
  2. Shoulder straps: snug enough to hug your shoulders without taking most of the weight.
  3. Load lifters: on larger packs, the small straps above your shoulders should angle back at roughly 45 degrees.
  4. Sternum strap: about an inch below your collarbones, loose enough to breathe deeply.
  5. Walk it: climb a staircase. Any rubbing now becomes a sore spot after 15 km.

Why does the hip belt matter on a hiking backpack?

The hip belt matters because your legs and hips carry weight far better than your shoulders. On any pack above about 30 litres, a padded hip belt that wraps the top of your hip bones makes the difference between a comfortable day and a sore back.

On a small daypack a thin webbing belt is fine, as it only stops the pack swinging. When you try bigger hiking backpacks in Nairobi, the padding should cover the top of your hip bones. If the belt sits on your waist or slides to your thighs, the torso size is wrong.

What Should You Look for When Buying Hiking Backpacks in Nairobi?

When buying hiking backpacks in Nairobi, check fit first, then the back panel, hip belt, zips, buckles, fabric and pockets. Five minutes of hands-on checking tells you more than a brand logo.

Are thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi worth buying?

Thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi are worth buying when the frame, hip belt, zips and buckles are sound. A well-made pack from a good brand can last many years, so a pre-owned one often gives you better build quality for your budget than a cheap new pack.

Before you pay, open every zip, clip every buckle, tug the shoulder strap seams and look inside for flaking coating; a musty smell can mean damp storage. Our shop sells quality thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi alongside some new items, which puts a good pack within reach of most budgets.

Do you need a rain cover for your backpack?

Yes, carry some rain protection for your backpack on most Kenyan hikes, because few pack fabrics are fully waterproof at the seams and zips. A fitted rain cover or a liner inside the pack keeps your spare layers and phone dry.

A heavy-duty bin bag inside the pack works as a cheap liner, which helps because many hiking backpacks in Nairobi, new or thrifted, come without a cover. A waterproof rain poncho that drapes over both you and your pack is another option; our post on when a rain poncho beats a rain jacket explains the trade-offs.

How Should You Pack a Daypack for a Hike Near Nairobi?

Pack a daypack with heavy items close to your back and between your shoulder blades, soft items at the bottom, and rain gear and snacks where you can reach them in seconds. A balanced pack feels lighter than a badly packed one of the same weight.

Here is a worked example for a full day on Mt Longonot or the Ngong Hills ridge in a 25-28 litre daypack. The same order works for all hiking backpacks in Nairobi, from small hydration packs to 70 litre trekking packs.

Where in the packWhat goes thereWhy

Middle, against your back2-3 L of water (bladder or bottles), lunchThe heaviest items sit closest to your spine
TopRain jacket or poncho, first aid kitOut in seconds when a storm builds over the Rift
Lid or hip belt pocketsPhone, sunscreen, snacks, headlamp, ID and cashReachable without taking the pack off

How heavy should a day hiking pack be?

A day hiking pack is most comfortable at around 10% of your body weight or less, so 6-8 kg for most adults. Water makes up a big share of that weight.

Which Mistakes Do Hikers Make With Backpacks?

The most common mistakes with hiking backpacks in Nairobi and beyond are buying too big, wearing the hip belt too low, carrying heavy items at the bottom and leaving rain protection at home. Each one is easy to fix before your next hike.

  • Buying for the dream trip: a 65 litre pack bought "for Kilimanjaro one day" is clumsy on every Saturday day hike in between.
  • Hip belt on the waist: worn too high, the belt squeezes your stomach and the weight drops onto your shoulders.
  • Heavy items at the bottom or far from the back: this levers the pack away from you and makes scrambles feel unsteady.
  • No liner in the rainy season: in October and November, afternoon storms can soak a pack in minutes.

Pro Tips: Living With Your Pack

  • Adjust on the move: loosen the hip belt slightly on long descents and snug it up again on climbs
  • Re-tension after an hour: straps settle as the pack warms up, so give everything a small pull at the first break
  • Liner first, then gear: line the pack before loading so nothing gets missed in a sudden storm
  • Empty it the same evening: damp socks and banana peels left overnight are how packs start to smell

How Should You Care for a Hiking Backpack?

Care for a hiking backpack by emptying it after every hike, brushing out dust and grass seeds, and drying it fully in the shade. Hand wash it in lukewarm water with a mild, pH-neutral soap when it gets dirty, and never put it in a washing machine.

Deuter, a major pack maker, warns that a washing machine can damage the fabric and the polyurethane coating inside many packs, and advises against fabric softener, bleach and tumble dryers. Hang the pack upside down to dry with all zips open, away from direct sun and heaters, then store it somewhere dry rather than squashed under a bed in a damp corner. Deuter's backpack cleaning guide gives the full method, and it applies to most hiking backpacks in Nairobi whatever the brand.

Hiking backpacks in Nairobi take a beating from red dust and strong equatorial sun, so dry yours on a shaded line rather than a hot roof, and wipe the zips after dusty hikes such as Hell's Gate, because grit wears the sliders. Rinse a bladder after every hike and dry it open.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much should I spend on hiking backpacks in Nairobi?

Hiking backpacks in Nairobi deserve a bigger share of your budget than most items, because a pack that does not fit spoils every hike. Quality thrifted packs give you a well-made brand-name pack for less than a new one. Compare current prices on our product pages and pick the best-fitting pack you can afford, not the biggest or the cheapest.

Can I just use my school or laptop bag for a hike?

A school or laptop bag is fine for a short, flat walk in Karura Forest, but it is a poor choice for longer hikes. Laptop bags have no hip belt, no ventilated back and no side bottle pockets, so the weight hangs on your shoulders and your back gets soaked in sweat. Most 20-30 litre hiking backpacks in Nairobi shops are far more comfortable.

Is a water bladder better than bottles for hiking?

A water bladder is better for hot, steady hikes because you sip through a tube without stopping, which helps you drink enough. Bottles are easier to refill, clean and keep track of. Plenty of hiking backpacks in Nairobi have a bladder sleeve, so many hikers carry a 2-3 litre bladder plus one bottle in a side pocket for electrolytes.

Do women need a women's hiking backpack?

Women do not need a women's hiking backpack, but many find one more comfortable. Women's versions of hiking backpacks in Nairobi usually have a shorter torso, narrower curved shoulder straps and a more angled hip belt. The right choice is whichever pack matches your torso length and feels good when loaded, so try both styles with weight inside before you decide.

Final Thoughts

Volume first, fit second, condition third: get those three right and almost any hike near the city feels easier. For most people buying hiking backpacks in Nairobi, that means a well-fitted 25-30 litre daypack with sound zips and buckles, and a larger trekking pack only once you start camping or carrying your own kit on Mt Kenya.
